page: Amazon Web Services c8g.medium is a compute-optimized instance powered by a custom AWS Graviton processor. Built on the ARMv9 architecture and utilizing the Neoverse-V2 core model, this server features 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU running at 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography support. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of single-core efficiency and resource-constrained multi-core limits. In single-core stress-ng testing, the server achieves an average performance score of 1693.68, which matches its multi-core score due to the single-vCPU configuration. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is a strong point, reaching 14.02 GB/sec, while single-threaded gzip compression performs at an average rate of 30.01 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth is relatively constrained, with uncached read speeds at 30.05 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.61 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and database operations score in the lower percentiles, and Redis SET operations reach 2.38 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8g.medium offers a low-entry hardware profile for ARM64 development and testing. Its dedicated core allocation ensures predictable execution without CPU credit exhaustion, though the 2.0 GB memory capacity and lack of local storage limit its use for memory-intensive or data-heavy applications. This instance is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, microservices, ARM64 software compilation, basic web serving, and low-traffic API endpoints.
